architecture: GlmForCausalLM (native transformers, same tensors as glm-4-9b-chat converted by the model authors (their config.json has a WRONG rope_theta, see rope_note); GlmDecoderLayer x40; GQA 32q/2kv x 128)
params_note: total parameters as instantiated by transformers (meta device); checkpoint index reports 9399951360 (+32 = rotary inv_freq buffers)
active_params_note: dense model: all parameters are active
fits_single_80gb_detail: bf16: 18.8 GB weights, leaves ~60 GB for activations/KV on an 80 GB GPU
weights_gb_4bit_note: ESTIMATE (nf4 + double quant = ~0.52 B/param on nn.Linear weights, embeddings + lm_head stay bf16)

access_check.method: HfApi.model_info + HTTP HEAD (redirects not followed) with the local HF token on config.json and the first safetensors shard (2xx/3xx = accessible, 401/403 = gated and access not granted); no weights downloaded

license: glm-4 (custom license, HF 'other'): free for academic research, commercial use requires registration, no military/illegal use
min_transformers_note: GlmForCausalLM first appears in transformers v4.46.0 (GitHub tag check); verified on 4.57.6, 5.0.0, 5.24.0 with tiny models
thinking_note: no thinking mode in this model
max_new_note: defaults of the adapter (Ctx.run(max_new=...) overrides): cot 640, reasoning/thinking 2048 (hard GPQA-style questions can exceed it -> unparsed counts wrong, watch parse_rate), direct 8
layer_path_note: attribute path starting at the loaded model object (`model`), i.e. the adapter attribute layer_path is 'model.layers'
layer_path_verified: meta device on transformers 4.57.6: `model.model.layers` is a ModuleList of 40 GlmDecoderLayer == num_hidden_layers == 40, 9,399,951,360 params. Tiny random GlmForCausalLM on transformers 4.57.6/5.0.0/5.24.0: hidden_states[L] == output of layers[L-1] exactly for 1<=L<40; hidden_states[40] is post final-norm (avoid L=nl). Equivalence with the remote-code variant: the upstream conversion renames keys and splits the fused qkv (no q/k permutation); a tiny random remote ChatGLM (real config) and the native model holding its tensors give identical logits (max|dlogit| 0) at RoPE base 5,000,000 and clearly different ones (~7e-2) at the Hub config's 10000 (test test_hf_variant_equals_the_remote_code_variant_only_at_the_adapters_rope_base, transformers 4.57.6). Real 9B weights were not compared (not available locally): do not mix directions across the two keys without a check.
rope_note: THUDM/glm-4-9b-chat-hf/config.json says rope_theta=10000.0, but the original model (ChatGLM remote code: base = 10000 * rope_ratio, rope_ratio=500 in THUDM/glm-4-9b-chat/config.json) uses 5,000,000. Cause: upstream convert_glm_weights_to_hf.py (transformers v4.46.3 and main) computes `10000.0 * getattr(original_config, "rope_ratio", 1)` on a dict from json.load, which is always 1, so every converted Hub config says 10000 (also glm-4-9b-chat-1m-hf, whose original has rope_ratio 10000; glm-4-9b-hf is right because its original has no rope_ratio). All other mapped config fields agree with the original (checked). load() corrects the base and verifies it on the loaded model; see known_issues.
template_notes:
[gMASK]<sop><|system|>
{sys}<|user|>
{user}<|assistant|>  (system turn omitted when there is no framing text). The reply starts with '
' (training format '<|assistant|>
{reply}'); no thinking mode. eos ids [151329 <|endoftext|>, 151336 <|user|>, 151338 <|observation|>], pad = <|endoftext|>. Letters A..J are single tokens (ids 32..41). `tok(rendered, add_special_tokens=True)` would PREPEND a second '[gMASK]<sop>' (verified for the remote and the fast tokenizer): the adapter encodes with add_special_tokens=False and render() asserts exactly one prefix. The chat template is identical in glm-4-9b-chat and glm-4-9b-chat-hf and both tokenizers give identical ids. Rendered N prompt (toy question) = 67 tokens, E = 136 tokens.
known_issues: Same tensors as glm-4-9b-chat, converted to the native GlmForCausalLM (but NOT the same config: see the ROPE BASE entry); params differ by 32 (the rotary inv_freq buffers stored in the remote checkpoint). The tokenizer chat template and ids are identical to the remote variant (verified).
hidden_states[40] is post final-norm (native HF convention): avoid L=40 for directions. Layers 1..39 follow the SPEC convention exactly (verified on tiny models, transformers 4.57.6/5.0.0/5.24.0).

tok(text, add_special_tokens=True) prepends a second '[gMASK]<sop>' (the fast tokenizer's post-processor); adapter.encode uses add_special_tokens=False. tokenizer_config sets model_input_names=[input_ids, attention_mask] so no token_type_ids.

ROPE BASE (fixed by load()): the Hub config says rope_theta=10000.0 but the original model uses 5,000,000 = 10000 x rope_ratio 500 (rope_note). A plain AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained of this repo therefore computes a different function than glm-4-9b-chat (at 16 tokens distance 11 of the 32 rotary frequencies are off by more than 0.5 rad). load() reads the config first, sets the base (config.rope_theta on transformers 4.x; config.rope_parameters['rope_theta'] on >=5, where the rope_theta kwarg and a plain attribute are silently ignored), passes config= and verifies model.model.rotary_emb.inv_freq (RuntimeError on mismatch); a config that says anything other than 10000 (the bug) or 5e6 (a corrected copy) is refused. Do NOT load this repo with plain from_pretrained. Verified offline with tiny random models: remote ChatGLM (real config) vs native GlmForCausalLM holding its tensors (upstream key mapping, which renames keys and splits qkv without permuting rows) give identical logits at 5e6 (max|dlogit| 0) and differ by ~7e-2 at 1e4 (transformers 4.57.6). NOT verifiable offline: the accuracy cost of an uncorrected load on the real 9B weights, and equality of the real weights of the two repos.

Remote-code-free, so it is the only 9B key usable on transformers>=5 (needed when the pod also runs glm-4.7-flash); use it through this adapter's load() only, because of the RoPE base correction above.

cot mode: 'Think step by step briefly, then finish with a final line of the form Answer: <letter>'; parser takes the LAST explicit 'Answer: X' (also 'answer is X', \\boxed{X}, Chinese 答案：X); a reply that merely starts with 'A. ...' (truncated option list) is NOT parsed. Truncation at max_new=640 is scored as unparsed.

load() sets config.use_cache=False (and pins generation_config.use_cache=True): Ctx.hidden_last / Ctx.neutral_stats / check_convention call model(**enc, output_hidden_states=True) with HF's default use_cache=True and would otherwise allocate a full KV cache for a pure prefill (and they have no OOM fallback: only Ctx._gen_chunk splits batches on OOM). generate() is unaffected (identical texts, still uses its cache; verified on tiny models of every GLM family on transformers 4.57.6 / 5.0.0 / 5.24.0, see tests).
recommended_gpu: 1x A100/H100 80GB (bf16); a 24 GB GPU suffices for small batches. Works on transformers 4.46 .. 5.x (recommended: the remote-code variant needs a shim on 4.57 and is unusable on >=5).
hf_generate_speed: Dense 9.4B: HF generate roughly 20-35 tokens/s per sequence on one A100/H100 (ESTIMATE, unmeasured).
kv_note: bf16 bytes per token over all layers; true = what HF generate() allocates (adapter.kv_bytes_per_token probes it on the loaded model); core_formula = sbx.core.kv_bytes_per_token(model)

est_prompt_tokens.basis: measured with the real tokenizer + adapter.build over data/questions_heldout_eval.jsonl (400 four-option bio questions); long-context sets (labbench_*) are much longer

est_tokens_per_question_basis: ESTIMATE of generated tokens per 4-option bio MCQ in this key's mode (prior knowledge of how verbose these models are); NOT measured (no weights available locally). Replace with the mean generated length from the first GPU run.
greedy_only_note: core passes do_sample=False; load() additionally clears temperature/top_p/top_k in the generation_config (the repos ship sampling defaults)
estimates_unmeasured: est_tokens_per_question, hf_generate_speed and the 4-bit footprint are ESTIMATES: no weights/GPU were available to the adapter author. Everything else in this card (counts, paths, templates, versions, sizes) was measured/verified as described.
